mission: RED MODE - TEAM B (BACKEND) - Audit Mission Control API routes

findings.details: CORSMiddleware configured with allow_origins=['*'], which permits any website to access iHIM APIs. This is a major security vulnerability for local applications.
findings.impact: Malicious websites could trigger actions, spawn agents, restart server, access notes/tasks, or manipulate team state.

findings.details: The /api/terminal/dispatch endpoint uses shlex.quote() which is good, but the prompt is replaced with spaces instead of being properly escaped for multiline. The command is also sent directly to terminal without sanitization.
findings.impact: Attacker could inject shell commands via crafted prompts with special characters.
findings.recommendation: Add input validation, use subprocess with argument list instead of shell string, or implement proper prompt escaping.
findings.fixed: PARTIAL - shlex.quote() added but implementation could be stronger

findings.details: GET /api/actions correctly filters out actions with hidden=True flag. Verified that slash_commands, software_dev_team, and agent_team_builder are properly hidden from desktop.
findings.impact: None - this is working as intended.
findings.recommendation: No action needed. This is a POSITIVE finding.

findings.details: Slash commands router uses prefix '/api/slash-commands' (plural), team builder uses '/api/teams' (plural), but terminal uses '/api/terminal' (singular). Inconsistent naming convention.
findings.impact: Developer confusion, harder to remember endpoints.
findings.recommendation: Standardize to either all plural or all singular. Suggest: /api/terminals (plural) for consistency.

findings.details: Lines 1272-1297 provide comprehensive documentation of all available commands endpoints. This is a best practice.
findings.impact: Positive - makes API discoverable and maintainable.
findings.recommendation: Replicate this pattern for team builder and terminal routers.

findings.details: System uses FEEDBACK_AVAILABLE, SANITY_AVAILABLE, etc. flags with try/except imports. Returns helpful error messages when modules unavailable.
findings.impact: Positive - prevents crashes when optional modules missing.
findings.recommendation: No action needed. This is excellent error handling.

findings.issue: Slash commands API is comprehensive and well-designed
findings.details: The /api/slash-commands/* endpoints provide full CRUD for commands, ideas, categories, auto-invoke config, and sync. Includes filtering, search, and voting.
findings.impact: Positive - provides all functionality needed for command management.
findings.recommendation: No action needed. This is production-ready.

findings.details: Provides template CRUD, instance management, agent selection, and spawn endpoints. Protects built-in templates from deletion. Good separation of concerns.

findings.issue: Terminal API supports both winpty and subprocess backends
findings.details: WebSocket endpoint at /api/terminal/ws/{session_id} handles real-time I/O. Supports session management, scrollback, resize, and dispatching agents. Auto-creates sessions on connect.
findings.impact: Positive - flexible and feature-complete terminal implementation.

findings.issue: Server restart endpoint has security risks
findings.details: POST /api/server/restart kills ALL Python processes and restarts. No authentication. Accessible via CORS wildcard. Uses PowerShell with potential for injection.
findings.impact: Attacker could restart server repeatedly (DoS) or potentially inject PowerShell commands.
findings.recommendation: Add authentication, validate paths, restrict CORS first. Consider if this endpoint is necessary.

findings.issue: Team spawn endpoints lack rate limiting
findings.details: POST /api/team/spawn and /api/team/spawn-custom don't have rate limits. Could spawn unlimited agents rapidly.
findings.recommendation: Add rate limiting (e.g., max 5 spawns per minute) or concurrent team limit.

findings.issue: Stopwatches and tasks use file I/O on every request
findings.details: Every GET/POST loads and saves JSON files. No caching or in-memory state.
findings.impact: Minor performance overhead, but acceptable for small datasets.
findings.recommendation: Consider in-memory cache with periodic persistence if performance becomes an issue.

immediate: Fix CORS wildcard (SEC-001) - restrict to localhost only
Add authentication to server restart endpoint (SEC-003)
Add rate limiting to team spawn endpoints (VAL-001)
short_term: Strengthen command injection protection in terminal dispatch (SEC-002)
Standardize API route naming (singular vs plural) (API-002)
nice_to_have: Add inline documentation blocks for team_builder and terminal routers (DOC-001)
Consider caching for frequently-accessed data files (OPT-001)

mission_control_routes./api/terminal/sessions: GET - List sessions, POST - Create session
mission_control_routes./api/terminal/sessions/{id}: GET - Session details, DELETE - Kill session
mission_control_routes./api/terminal/dispatch: POST - Dispatch the agent agent in terminal

team_routes./api/teams/templates: GET - List templates, POST - Create template
team_routes./api/teams/templates/{id}: GET - Template details, PUT - Update, DELETE - Delete

slash_command_routes./api/slash-commands/ideas/{id}: GET - Idea details, PUT - Update, DELETE - Delete

notes: All three Mission Control modules (terminal, team_builder, slash_commands) are properly integrated
API is well-organized with clear separation of concerns
Error handling is generally good with graceful degradation
Main security concern is CORS wildcard - needs immediate attention
No critical functional bugs found - all endpoints appear to be working as designed
Documentation is good in some areas, could be improved in others
Terminal implementation is sophisticated with winpty fallback
